hints: Look carefully at the graph and notice the two separate features, the steepness at the start and the final plateau height.
Remember that the final volume of oxygen depends only on the starting moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, calculated by $n = c \times V$.
Connect initial steepness to rate, which is increased by higher concentration and by powdered catalyst, then match which curve is faster but finishes lower.
walkthrough:
**Read what X and Y tell us**

Curve Y starts steeper, so Y is faster. Curve X finishes higher, so X makes more total oxygen.

Think: slope = rate, plateau = total moles of product.

**Link final volume to moles of H2O2**

$\text{MnO}_2$ is a catalyst, so it does not change the total gas. The total $\text{O}_2$ comes only from $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ used up.

$$n(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2) = \text{concentration} \times \text{volume}$$

**Link initial rate to concentration and surface area**

A higher $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ concentration gives more frequent collisions and a faster rate. Powdered $\text{MnO}_2$ has a larger surface area than lumps, so it also gives a faster rate.

So the faster curve Y must have the higher concentration and the powder.

**Test the numbers**

For the correct row, X: $50 \text{ cm}^3 \times 0.1 \text{ mol dm}^{-3} = 0.0050 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$. Y: $20 \text{ cm}^3 \times 0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3} = 0.0040 \text{ mol}$.

X has more moles, so higher plateau. Y has double the concentration plus powder, so faster start. This matches X slow and high, Y fast and low perfectly.

options.A: X has $50 \times 0.1 = 5$ mmol and Y has $50 \times 0.2 = 10$ mmol, so Y would finish higher. The graph shows X finishes higher, so this is reversed. Y is correctly faster due to powder and higher concentration, but the total volumes are wrong.
options.B: X has $25 \times 0.2 = 5$ mmol and Y has $25 \times 0.1 = 2.5$ mmol, so X finishing higher is correct. However X has powder and higher concentration, so X would be faster, but the graph shows Y is faster. The rate prediction is the wrong way round.
options.C: X has $50 \times 0.1 = 5.0$ mmol, Y has $20 \times 0.2 = 4.0$ mmol, so X produces more $\text{O}_2$ and has the higher plateau. Y has $0.2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ and powdered $\text{MnO}_2$ versus $0.1 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ and lumps for X, so Y reacts faster with a steeper start. Both features match the graph.
options.D: X has $20 \times 0.2 = 4$ mmol and Y has $40 \times 0.1 = 4$ mmol, so both would give the same final volume of $\text{O}_2$. The graph shows clearly different plateaus with X higher, so equal moles cannot be correct.
